Daveigh Elizabeth Chase (née Chase-Schwallier; July 24, 1990 – June 16, 2026) was an Annie Award-winning American actress, singer, and voice over artist best known for playing Chihiro Ogino in the English adaptation of Spirited Away, Rhonda Volmer in the HBO series Big Love, Samara Morgan in The Ring and Lilo Pelekai in Lilo & Stitch.

14892: Rosemarie Braddock DeWitt (born October 26, 1971) is an American actress. DeWitt played Emily Lehman in the Fox television series Standoff (2006–07), co-starring with her future husband Ron Livingston, as well as Charmaine Craine on United States of Tara. She also was the title character in 2008's Rachel Getting Married, garnering several awards and nominations for best supporting actress. She starred in the horror/thriller Poltergeist (2015), a remake of the 1982 film of the same name.
Flushing, Queens, New York City, New York, USA
15148:
Jon Amiel (born 20 May 1948) is an English director who has worked in film and television in both the UK and the US. After receiving a BAFTA Award nomination for the BBC series The Singing Detective (1986), he went on to direct films, including Sommersby (1993), Copycat (1995), Entrapment (1999), The Core (2003) and Creation (2009).

Description above from the Wikipedia article Jon Amiel, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.
16940:
Jeremy John Irons (born 19 September 1948) is an English actor and activist. After receiving classical training at the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School, Irons began his acting career on stage in 1969 and has appeared in many West End theatre productions, including the Shakespeare plays The Winter's Tale, Macbeth, Much Ado About Nothing, The Taming of the Shrew and Richard II. In 1984, he made his Broadway debut in Tom Stoppard's The Real Thing, receiving the Tony Award for Best Actor in a Play.

Irons's break-out role came in the ITV series Brideshead Revisited (1981) and is frequently ranked among the greatest British television dramas as well as greatest literary adaptations.
Cowes, Isle of Wight, England, UK
19244: Michael Robert Winner was a British film director, producer and food critic. He is perhaps best known for directing several movies starring Charles Bronson, including three of the five Death Wish films.
31532: William Joshua Hopkins is an American actor, best known as Raymond Millbury on Ally McBeal, Grayson Ellis on Cougar Town, and Liam O'Connor on Quantico.
32300:
Johnny Harris first burst onto our screens in 2006 in the highly acclaimed British film London to Brighton. The film was voted into Time Out Magazine’s ‘100 Greatest British Films of All Time’ and celebrated British director Shane Meadows said of Harris’ performance in the film: “It’s an incredibly bold and massively powerful performance, the best I’ve seen on celluloid for a long time.”

He went on to star in Shane Meadows cult television series This Is England ’86 receiving BAFTA and Royal Television Society Award nominations for his performance.
37932:
Felix Gary Gray (born July 17, 1969) is an American director and producer. Gray began his career as a director on numerous critically acclaimed and award-winning music videos, including "It Was a Good Day" by Ice Cube, "Natural Born Killaz" by Dr. Dre and Ice Cube, "Keep Their Heads Ringin'" by Dr. Dre, "Waterfalls" by TLC, and "Ms. Jackson" by Outkast.

Gray made his feature-film directorial debut with the comedy Friday (1995). He has since directed the films Set It Off (1996), The Negotiator (1998), The Italian Job (2003), Be Cool (2005), Law Abiding Citizen (2009), and Straight Outta Compton (2015).
New York City, New York, USA
58924:
Clifton Powell (born 16 March 1956 in Washington, D.C., USA) – American actor and comedian, who grew up in the Mayfair Mansions housing project in Northeast D.C. and graduated from the Duke Ellington School of the Arts before studying at Emerson College in Boston.  He is married with two children and two grandchildren.

His most notable film roles include Menace II Society (1993), Dead Presidents (1995), Rush Hour (1998) as Luke, Next Friday (2000) and Friday After Next (2002) as Pinky, Ray (2004) as Jeff Brown (NAACP Image Award nomination for Outstanding Supporting Actor), Norbit (2007), Street Kings (2008), and All Eyez on Me (2017).
78124: François Civil (born 29 January 1990) is a French actor. He has appeared in both French and English-language productions and is known for his roles in films such as Frank (2014), As Above, So Below (2014), Five (2016), Burn Out (2017), Love at Second Sight (2019), The Wolf's Call (2019), Who You Think I Am (2019), Someone, Somewhere (2019), BAC Nord (2021), for voicing Buzz Lightyear in the French version of the animated film Lightyear (2022), and for playing D'Artagnan in The Three Musketeers: D'Artagnan (2023) and The Three Musketeers: Milady (2023). On television, he has starred in the Disney Channel teen sitcom series Trop la Classe!
82732:
Mohanlal Vishwanathan Nair known mononymously as Mohanlal is an Indian actor, producer and singer who is well known for his versatile and natural acting in Indian cinema. He made his acting debut in the unreleased movie Thiranottam (1978), which was followed by a role as the lead antagonist in his first release Manjil Virinja Pookkal in 1980, his onscreen debut.

Antagonistic parts in several movies followed before Mohanlal established himself as a lead actor playing a wide variety of character types in comedy and action films amongst others. He was labelled a superstar of Malayalam cinema in 1986 after the success of Rajavinte Makan, in which he played an underworld don.
85036:
Minissha Lamba (born on 18 January 1985) is an Indian actress who appears in Bollywood films. She has appeared in Yahaan, Bachna Ae Haseeno, Kidnap and Well Done Abba.

Description above from the Wikipedia article Minissha Lamba  licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.
86060:
Shilpa Shetty Kundra (born Ashwini Shetty, 8 June 1975) is an Indian film actress and model. Since making her debut in the film Baazigar (1993), she has appeared in nearly 40 Bollywood, Tamil, and Kannada films, her first leading role being in the 1994 Aag. Although she has been through years of decline during her career, Shetty has been willing to reinvent herself quite often. Her performances in Dhadkan (2000) and Rishtey (2002) were appreciated, while her portrayal of an AIDS patient in Phir Milenge (2004) won her many accolades. Her younger sister Shamita Shetty is also a Bollywood film actress.

Shetty has been embroiled in various controversies including suspected mafia links.
93228:
Louis Herthum (born July 5, 1956) is an American actor and producer. Herthum has worked as a stage, television, and film actor, and he has also appeared in national television commercials. He is best known for his recurring role as Dep. Andy Broom on Murder, She Wrote and Peter Abernathy in the HBO television series Westworld.

Description above from the Wikipedia article Louis Herthum, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.
93996: Jang Young-nam (장영남) is a South Korean actress. She was born on November 25, 1973.
123180: Raveena Tandon (born 26 October 1974) is an Indian actress, model and producer who works in Hindi films. She is the daughter of director Ravi Tandon, and was born and raised in Mumbai. She started her career in modelling and later made her acting debut in the 1991 action film Patthar Ke Phool, which won her the Filmfare Award for New Face of the Year.
139820:
Pom Alexandra Klementieff (French: [pɔmklemɑ̃tjɛf]; born 3 May 1986) is a French actress. She is best known for playing Mantis in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) since 2017 and an assassin in Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning Part One (2023).

Description above from the Wikipedia article Pom Klementieff, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.
142636:
Josh Lee Holloway (born July 20, 1969) is an American actor best known for his roles as James "Sawyer" Ford on the television show Lost and as Will Bowman on the science fiction drama Colony. Most recently he had a recurring role in season 3 of the western series Yellowstone.

Holloway was born in San Jose, California, the second of four boys of a nurse mother and a surveyor father. His family moved to the Blue Ridge Mountains of Georgia when he was two. He was raised in Free Home, Georgia. Holloway is related to Baptist preacher Dr. Dale Holloway, and author and World War II prisoner of war Carl Holloway. He is also a descendant of Robert E. Lee.
156204: Constance Zimmer (born October 11, 1970) is an American actress perhaps best known for her role as Dana Gordon in HBO's Entourage and as Claire Simms on the critically acclaimed ABC legal comedy-drama Boston Legal. She also starred on NBC's short-lived series Love Bites. From 2013 to 2014, she starred in the Netflix original series House of Cards. She currently stars in the upcoming television series UnREAL that premiered on Lifetime in June 2015.
229932: Golshifteh Farahani (گلشیفته فراهانی) was born on 10th July 1983 and is an international Iranian actress. Golshifteh Farahani started her acting career in theatre at the age of 6. Since then she has played in more than 40 films, many of which have been screened or awarded at international festivals. Amongst her famous Iranian films are Bahman Ghobadi's Half Moon, Dariush Mehrjui's Santoori , Rasool Mollagholipour's M for Mother and Asghar Farhadi's About Elly. Starring in Ridley Scotts Body of Lies (2008), alongside Leonardo Di Caprio and Russel Crowe, Golshifteh Farahani became the first Iranian to act in a major Hollywood production.
237612:
Namitha (born May 10, 1981) is an Indian actress who works primarily in Tamil and Telugu cinema, alongside appearances in Kannada, Malayalam, and Hindi films.

She entered the entertainment industry after competing in pageantry, finishing as the third runner-up at Femina Miss India 2001. She made her acting debut in Telugu cinema in 2002 with Sontham and Gemeni. Her subsequent Telugu appearances included Oka Raju Oka Rani (2003) and Oka Radha Iddaru Krishnula Pelli (2003).

In 2004, she made her Tamil film debut in Engal Anna, followed by Aai (2004) and Maha Nadigan (2004).
515628: Sofia Black-D'Elia (born December 24, 1991) is an American actress. She is known for her work in television series, including Skins, Gossip Girl, The Night Of, Your Honor, The Mick, and Single Drunk Female. She also starred in the films Project Almanac (2015), Viral (2016), and Remarkably Bright Creatures (2026).
1057068: Han Ye-ri is a South Korean film and television actress.
1136940:
Lili Reinhart (born September 13, 1996) is an American actress. She is known for portraying Betty Cooper on The CW teen drama series Riverdale (2017–2023) and Annabelle in Lorene Scafaria's black comedy crime drama film Hustlers.

Description above from the Wikipedia article Lili Reinhart, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.
1324588: Genki Muro (室 元気, Muro Genki, July 31, 1989) is a Japanese voice actor from Miyagi Prefecture. He is currently affiliated with Remax, and previously was with Production Baobab and Space Craft Entertainment.
1336108: Gobinath Chandran is an Indian television anchor, radio jockey, journalist, reporter, news presenter/moderator, entrepreneur, writer and an author, currently featured on the STAR Vijay debate show Neeya Naana.
1386540: Ryu Hye-young (born March 28, 1991) is a South Korean actress and model. She is known for her role as Sung Bo-ra in the hit drama series Reply 1988 (2015-2016), Shim Eun-Joo in Dear My Room (2018) and as Kang Sol A in the recent drama series Law School (2021).
1448492: Castille Landon was born in Bradenton, Florida, USA, the daughter of Dori A. Rath. She is a director and writer, known for Fear of Rain (2021), After We Fell (2021) and After Ever Happy (2022).
1453100:
Samuel Nicholas Wechsler is an American actor in both TV and theater. He is known for his roles as Kyle Valenti on The WB teen drama series Roswell and Jack Porter on the ABC drama television series Revenge.  He has went on to land recurring roles in such series as "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia," "Without a Trace" and "Vanished," as well as guest starring roles in "Chase," "Past Life," "The Sarah Connor Chronicles," "Crossing Jordan," "Cold Case," "Tru Calling," "Malcolm in the Middle" and in the made-for-television movie "Perfect Game."

As a thespian truly dedicated to his craft, Nick has vast experience in theatre.
1510444: Diamond White (born September 19, 1999) is an American singer, actress and voice actress who, in 2007 at the age of 8, starred in a Chicago-based production of The Color Purple that also toured nationally. She voices Frankie Greene in Transformers: Rescue Bots, Fuli on the Disney Junior series The Lion Guard, and has had cameo appearances on The Haunted Hathaways and Sofia the First and a recurring role on Phineas and Ferb. In 2012, she was a contestant on the second season of the American version of The X Factor, finishing in fifth place.
1660716:
T. A. Madhuram (Tamil: டி. ஏ. மதுரம்; 1918–November 27, 1974) was a Tamil stage and film actress and Tamil film producer

Madhuram was born in Srirangam in 1918 in a family of artists. Her first break in Tamil films, however, occurred only in 1935, after she had married N. S. Krishnan.
1885228: Daniel Doheny is a Canadian actor known for starring in the 2017 Canadian comedy film Adventures in Public School and the 2018 Netflix films Alex Strangelove, a coming-of-age story, and The Package, a raunchy comedy.
2085676: Mainak Bhaumik (born 15 January) is a Bengali film director and editor, whose directorial debut Aamra (2006) was a moderate success. After a gap of six years, he directed the 2012 film Bedroom, followed by Maach Mishti & More, Ami Aar Amar Girlfriends and Family Album. In 2014, he had written and directed the drama movie Take One. His 2017 directorial venture includes the comedy-drama Bibaho Diaries starring Ritwick Chakraborty, Sohini Sarkar and Biswanath Basu. His 2018 projects include Ghare & Baire, Crisscross and Generation Ami. His 2019 releases include Bhoot Chaturdashi and Bornoporichoy. His 2022 releases include Kuler Achaar.
